title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Transmitting the Notice of the Ministry of Justice on Re-entrusting 23 Hong Kong Lawyers to Handle Notarization Affairs and Changing the Certification Method

articles.content_en: III. After the increase in the number of entrusted lawyers, the scope of notarization business handled by Hong Kong lawyers shall still be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Article 3 of the Notice on Certain Issues Concerning the Entrustment of Eight Hong Kong Lawyers to Handle Notarization (Document No. [85] Si Fa Gong Zi No. 251) issued by our Ministry on June 11, 1985, that is, in addition to handling certificates used by Hong Kong residents returning to the mainland for civil legal matters, they may also handle various certifying documents required by Hong Kong companies and organizations for handling economic legal affairs in the mainland, such as certificates of company creditworthiness, certificates of company articles of association, powers of attorney for signing economic contracts on behalf of others, certificates of company tax payment, bank guarantee certificates, and various certifying documents required by Hong Kong companies for litigation in the People's Court or arbitration in arbitration institutions in the mainland.

IV. After the increase in the number of entrusted lawyers, the total number of entrusted lawyers reaches 48, making it difficult to identify notarial certificates by the original method and also creating opportunities for a few lawless elements to produce forged notarial certificates. In order to facilitate the accurate identification of certificates issued by entrusted lawyers by the document-using units, the procedures for handling certificates by all entrusted Hong Kong lawyers shall, in addition to continuing to be handled in accordance with Article 1, paragraph 2, and Article 2 of the Notice on Certain Issues Concerning the Entrustment of Eight Hong Kong Lawyers to Handle Notarization (Document No. [85] Si Fa Gong Zi No. 251) issued by our Ministry, add a procedure, that is, after the entrusted lawyer signs and seals the notarial certificate, the certificate must pass through the Shenzhen Office of the "China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd." established by our Ministry and the CCPIT in Hong Kong, which shall affix a forwarding seal on the original notarial document before it may be taken to the mainland for use. The signature seals and chops of the entrusted lawyers shall no longer be filed with the notarial offices and relevant departments. The work of affixing the forwarding seal by the Shenzhen Office of China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. shall come into force on December 1, 1991. Please send the forwarding seal impression of the company to all relevant units for filing.
The above notice shall be promptly forwarded to the relevant departments of the people's governments of all cities, counties, and districts.
